reasons: New signal: exofop_tois, exofop_ctois and published_signal are all empty, and the verification record reports no TOI, CTOI, TCE or TESS EB match in the catalogues of 2026-10-15. Nothing here argues for a drop on grounds of prior knowledge.

The dip is recovered independently of the QLP sector-98 detection: other_sector_results gives S106 SPOC SNR 14.0 (expected 10.3) and S107 SPOC SNR 11.8 (expected 11.4); joint_search_snr 11.8 against joint_search_highest_null_snr 7.0 with joint_search_detected True; fit_depth_ppm 352 +/- 31; odd_even_difference_sigma 0.07; sector_depth_consistency_p_value 0.406 (depth_ppm_by_sector S98 375 +/- 41, S106 265 +/- 74, S107 372 +/- 71).

The fitted body is planet-sized and the geometry is consistent with a transit of the target: planet_radius_earth_radii 3.91 +/- 0.23 (far below the 22.4 stellar limit), transit_grazing False, fit_impact_parameter 0.450 +/- 0.2883, stellar_density_fit_to_tic_ratio 1.32, fitted_to_expected_scaled_semi_major_axis 0.74. gaia_ruwe 1.16, gaia_non_single_star 0 and gaia_eclipsing_binary False give no sign of a stellar companion.

The ellipsoidal caution is physically incompatible with the planet interpretation and cannot be dismissed with the present data: ellipsoidal_amplitude_ppm 126 +/- 31 (4 sigma; ellipsoidal_amplitude_ppm_by_sector S98 48 +/- 108, S106 129 +/- 43, S107 137 +/- 48) implies ellipsoidal_companion_mass_solar_masses 0.00332, about 3.5 Jupiter masses, which a 3.91 Earth-radius body cannot have. Either the P/2 term is stellar variability or the dip is not a planet. Gaia RV cannot separate these: gaia_rv_companion_mass_upper_limit_solar_masses 0.0707 is twenty times above 0.0033, and gaia_rv_variable False carries little weight because gaia_vbroad_km_s 270.8 makes the epoch RVs imprecise (gaia_rv_epoch_scatter_km_s 7.66).

The star is a very rapid rotator with strong coherent pulsation, and this is the main open question that no automatic step tests. gaia_vbroad_km_s 270.8 with stellar_radius_solar_radii 1.93 points to a hot, fast-rotating star. The all-sector figure tic121564843_0.81803.png shows oscillations of roughly 2000 ppm peak-to-peak with a period of about 1.2 h in the binned points of all three sector panels and in the phase-0.5 panel, where S98, S106 and S107 overlap in phase. A pulsation that folds coherently at 0.818 d across sectors months apart has a frequency commensurate with the candidate period, so the BLS period, the 352 ppm box dip (fit_duration_hours 2.358, about two pulsation cycles) and the P/2 ellipsoidal term can all be products of the pulsation rather than of a companion. The pulsation amplitude is several times the transit depth, so the independent SPOC recoveries in S106 and S107 do not exclude this, since they would find the same commensurate period.

Pixel check: pixel_verdict unresolved, joint_difference_image_snr 5.4, joint_best_source Gaia DR3 2978034081419676416, with per-sector SNRs 4.0 / 2.5 / 3.0 / 3.0 in pixel_verdicts_by_sector and an IndexError for S109. In the figures, S98 and S107 put the difference signal on the target pixel with the free-fit cross at or next to the target star; S106 and S108 are dominated by large-scale gradients and carry no information. I disagree with the weight the mechanical decision gives the 'dip can be on a nearby star' reason: gaia_neighbours_able_to_cause_dip says the G 18.9 star at 39 arcsec needs an 88% eclipse, which is implausible, and nfpp_mean is 0. The pixel data neither resolve nor seriously threaten the candidate; the pulsation and ellipsoidal terms are the real concern.

TRICERATOPS: fpp_mean 3.163e-09, nfpp_mean 0, most_likely_scenario TP on TIC 121564843, nearby_scenarios_excluded False. I give this little weight because TRICERATOPS assumes the dip is an astrophysical transit or eclipse on the target or a catalogued neighbour; it does not model a pulsation-induced false alarm, which is the hypothesis in question.

What would decide it: (a) unreleased_tess_sectors_observing_the_star 108 109 — adding the S108 and S109 SPOC light curves to step 9 (sectors_used is currently 98 106 107; cutout_depth_ppm_by_sector_and_aperture already gives S108 r1.5 11 +/- 158 and r2.0 7 +/- 163 ppm, consistent with zero but not conclusive) tests whether a 352 ppm dip persists at the propagated fit_epoch_btjd 4240.28625 and fit_period_days 0.8179751, and fixing the S109 pixel IndexError raises the joint difference-image SNR; (b) prewhitening the pulsation modes in S98, S106 and S107 and repeating the search and fit: if 1/0.818 d is a harmonic or combination of the pulsation frequencies, or the dip does not survive on a flat baseline, drop; if a 352 ppm box dip survives and the P/2 ellipsoidal amplitude falls to zero, propose for submission.

This matches the earlier decision recorded in the verification record on 2026-10-16 04:09 (held); I concur with it and with the mechanical 'held', but for the ellipsoidal and pulsation reasons rather than for the nearby-star reason.
